text:
sara: Quick sync — ran a cross-region microbenchmark for 30B and 70B on H100 vs A100. trying to figure Dedicated pool sizing for predictable tail latencies. link to raw csv: https://short.internal/runs/1765

tim: can you drop the p50/p90/p99 and concurrent reqs per GPU? that's the key for sizing.

anika: summary: H100 int8 gives ~1.9x tokens/s vs a100 int8 on decode-heavy workloads. p99 delta narrows when prefill ratio >0.25.

mateo: for Dedicated we should size for 95th percentile concurrency not mean. real traffic bursts drive queuing. proposing per-pool target_util 0.6 and burst runway 1.8x.

jess: curious about warmup. how long to get KV cache effective for chat-style sessions? that affects effective throughput for steady vs burst.

anika: KV prewarm TTL ~45s in our tests; after ~3 exchange turns throughput stabilizes. cold-fill cost is ~15-25% higher latency for first decode.

tim: numbers I pulled from the CSV: US-WEST1 H100 30B int8 @ concurrency=8 -> tokens/s 9200, p50 28ms, p90 120ms, p99 310ms. A100 same config -> tokens/s 4800, p50 55ms, p90 210ms, p99 450ms.

mateo: ok. so one H100 equiv ~= 1.9 A100 for this workload. For safety margin we should translate SLOs to GPU counts with a buffer for cross-az failover.

sara: propose math: target_concurrency_per_gpu = 10 for 30B decode-heavy (since batch packing helps). margin factor = 1.6 for burst runway + 1.1 for AZ failover -> overall 1.76. rounding up.

jess: can we also factor autoscale cooldowns? aggressive scale down causes oscillation during multi-minute bursts. current cooldown=60s is too short.

tim: agree. recommended autoscale snippet I tested:
```
policy: target_utilization: 0.62
scale_step: 1
max_scale_factor: 3.0
cooldown_seconds: 180
stabilization_window: 240
grace_capacity: 2
```
This keeps tail stable while letting us add capacity within ~3m.

anika: one more thing — quant spillover: when memory quantization pushes kernel choice from fused-attn -> tiled-attn we saw p99 jump by 2x. so pick quant profiles that avoid kernel fallback in the common-seqlen range.

mateo: region differences: eu-west1 shows ~10% higher p99 vs us-west1 for same hardware because of hotter network hop counts on our infra. asia-east1 is ~20% worse under load. We should bake region multiplicative factors into sizing tables.

sara: actionables: 1) create Dedicated sizing table: rows = {region, gpu_type, model_size}, cols = {concurrency_per_gpu, gpus_required_for_1k_rps, margin_factor}. 2) default margin_factor per region: us-west1=1.6, eu-west1=1.75, asia-east1=1.9. 3) default autoscale policy snippet above.

tim: I'll draft the table. rough calc: for 30B decode-heavy target 1k concurrent requests (average tokens per request ~120): on H100 concurrency_per_gpu=10 -> gpus_raw=100 -> with us-west1 margin 1.6 -> 160 GPUs. On A100 use conversion 1 H100 = 1.9 A100 -> need ~304 A100.

jess: that's a big difference for reserved capacity cost. maybe we offer mixed-pool config: base committed H100 for baseline throughput + burstable A100 spot for overflow. cheaper but riskier.

anika: mixed pools are fine but watch kernel parity: if H100 runs fused kernels and A100 falls back to tiled, outputs can have subtle latency artifacts during overflow. need automated fallback policy: prefer same-kernel siblings for overflow where possible.

mateo: ops-bot FYI: I'll open runbook PR with these thresholds and add an alert if scale_steps >2 within 10m (indicates under-provisioned baseline).

ops-bot: runbook PR created: https://git.internal/rb/5678 - watchers: @sara @tim @mateo

sara: thanks. last Q: do we want different sizing for chat vs single-turn completions? chat = smaller prefill ratio but long tail. single-turn = bigger prefill. i'd treat chat as more bursty and increase margin + add KV-warmup slots.

tim: agreed. chat pools: target_concurrency_per_gpu = 8, margin +0.15. single-turn pools: concurrency_per_gpu = 12.

jess: i'll model cost for both variants and share estimates.

anika: linking perf note: kernel selection matrix we used: fused-attn (preferred on H100), tiled-attn (A100 fallback), quant_profile v2-int8 and v3-int4. v3-int4 gives 30% lower memory but p99 regressions on long seqs. use v2-int8 as default for dedicated.

mateo: final ask: add a hard cap for max_scale_factor per pool to avoid runaway billing. current default 3x seems okay but for large base pools maybe cap absolute GPUs added to +50.

sara: great. i'll take ownership to convert this into the sizing doc and assign follow-ups. thanks everyone. :tada:
